# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 38 RED ROSES

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

That August, bees frequented the garden of the small dwelling, which was made red by late-blooming roses. Its inhabitants spent a great deal of time there, often eating picnic suppers in the lawn-covered space past the stream and lounging in it during the dusk hours as large night moths glided across the soft darkness. Adrian Treleaven discovered Lorna by herself in it one night. Nell and Hugh had gone out, while Tabitha, whose return was anticipated that evening, was still absent.
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0000 }

Above the fir summits, the northern sky displayed tones of amber and light green. August was drawing close to September, making the air chilly, so Lorna had draped a crimson scarf above her white dress. Side by side, without speaking, they walked along the small, welcoming paths packed with flowers. Adrian was obliged to depart before long. His time off had almost come to an end. Lorna sensed her heart pounding furiously. She was aware that this cherished garden would serve as the setting for the binding spoken vows that had to finalize their currently unspoken agreement.
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0001 }

“On certain nights an odd smell drifts along the breeze in this garden, resembling a ghostlike scent,” remarked Adrian. “From which exact flower it originates, I have never managed to find out. It is evasive, lingering, and remarkably sweet. I enjoy imagining that it is the spirit of Grandmother Tremayne dropping by for a brief call to the ancient place she adored so much. Plenty of welcoming phantoms ought to linger around this small aged dwelling.”
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0002 }

“Though I have resided beneath its roof for merely a month,” Lorna said, “my affection for it surpasses any love I felt for the house across the way, where my entire life was spent.”
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0003 }

“Love was the foundation upon which this home was constructed and blessed,” Adrian remarked. “Dwellings like this are BOUND to affect their inhabitants. Consider this garden, too—it has existed for more than six decades, with its flowers recording a thousand moments of anticipation and delight. Certain blossoms were in fact planted by the bride of the schoolmaster, who passed away three decades ago. Even so, their blooms return each summer. Observe those red roses, Lorna—they reign supreme over all the rest!”
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0004 }

“I adore the red roses,” Lorna stated. “Nell prefers the pink ones, whereas Hugh favors the white. However, I desire the crimson ones. No other flower fulfills a particular longing within me the way they do.”
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0005 }

“These roses arrive so late—their blossoms appear when every other flower has faded—and they preserve the entire heat and essence of the summer at its peak,” Adrian remarked, picking several of the vibrant, opening buds.
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0006 }

“For ages, humanity has recognized the rose as the emblem of affection. While love that is full of hope and anticipation is embodied by pink roses, and love that has been abandoned or perished is signified by white roses, the red ones—tell me, Lorna, what do red roses represent?”
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0007 }

“Love triumphant,” Lorna said softly.
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0008 }

“Indeed—affection victorious and faultless. Lorna, you are aware—you comprehend. I have adored you since the beginning. And I KNOW you adore me—I have no necessity to inquire of you. Yet I desire to listen to you state it—my precious—my precious!”
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0009 }

Lorna uttered words with an extremely quiet and shaking tone. Touch united their lips and hands; this represented the ultimate instance of their lives, and while they remained in that ancient garden, which possessed a long history of affection, joy, grief, and splendor, her glowing hair was adorned by him using the intensely red rose of victorious affection.
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0010 }

Shortly thereafter, Nell and Hugh came back, with Captain Saul alongside them. Because she loved the pixy flames, Nell set fire to a couple of driftwood sticks in the hearth, and they gathered about it to enjoy an hour of friendly company.
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0011 }

“Viewing a fire made of driftwood makes it simple for me to feel like I am youthful once more,” Captain Saul remarked.
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0012 }

“Are you able to foresee what lies ahead within the flames, Captain Saul?” Adrian inquired.
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0013 }

Captain Saul gazed with affection at everyone present, after which his eyes returned to Lorna's expressive features and shining eyes.
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0014 }

“To read your futures, I don’t need the fire,” he said. “For every one of you, I see happiness—for all of you—for Lorna and Mr. Treleaven—and the doctor here and Mistress Carrow—and Little Kit—and children who are not yet born but will be. Happiness for all of you—though, remember, I expect you will also have your troubles and worries and sorrows. They are sure to arrive—and no house, whether a palace or a little house of dreams, is able to bar ’em out. However, provided you face ’em TOGETHER with love and trust, they won’t get the better of you. With those two for compass and pilot, you can weather any storm.”
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0015 }

The aged man abruptly stood up, resting a hand upon the head of Lorna and another upon that of Nell.
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0016 }

“A pair of good, sweet women,” he remarked. “Loyal and devoted and worthy of trust. On account of you, your husbands will receive honor in the gates—in the time ahead, your children will stand up and proclaim you blessed.”
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0017 }

A peculiar gravity hung over the small gathering. Receiving a blessing, Nell and Lorna inclined their heads. Hugh abruptly wiped his eyes with his hand; Adrian Treleaven was absorbed like a person beholding visions. A period of silence fell upon everyone. To its repository of recollections, the small dwelling of visions attached yet another deeply moving and indelible instance.
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0018 }

“Now I need to depart,” Captain Saul finally uttered in a deliberate manner. Picking up his hat, he cast a long, reluctant gaze around the chamber.
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0019 }

“Good night, every one of you,” he remarked while leaving.
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0020 }

Nell was struck by the exceptional melancholy in his goodbye, prompting her to hurry to the doorway in his wake.
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0021 }

“Return shortly, Captain Saul,” she shouted, while he went past the small gate suspended in the middle of the fir trees.
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0022 }

“Ay, ay,” he answered her in a cheerful voice. Captain Saul, however, had occupied his place beside the familiar hearth in the house of dreams for the final time.
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0023 }

Nell returned to the rest of the group with deliberate steps.
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0024 }

“To imagine him traveling entirely by himself to that solitary Point is just so—so tragic,” she remarked. “Plus, nobody is present to greet him upon his arrival.”
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0025 }

“Captain Saul provides such pleasant fellowship to everyone else that his own presence must surely be agreeable to him,” Adrian remarked. “He has to experience solitude frequently, however. This evening, he resembled a prophet somewhat—his words sounded like those of a person granted a special message. In any case, I need to depart now as well.”
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0026 }

Nell and Hugh quietly slipped out of sight; nevertheless, after Adrian’s departure, Nell came back and discovered Lorna beside the fireplace.
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0027 }

“Oh, Lorna—I am aware—and it brings me such happiness, darling,” she stated, encircling her in a hug.
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0028 }

“My joy terrifies me, Nell,” Lorna murmured softly. “Its magnitude feels impossible—I fear giving it voice—or dwelling on it. I feel as though this is merely one more illusion born of this dwelling of phantoms, bound to disappear the moment I depart.”
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0029 }

“Indeed, you shall not depart from this spot—before Adrian comes to fetch you. Up to the arrival of that moment, you will remain in my company. Is it your belief that I would allow you to return to that desolate, gloomy location?”
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0030 }

“I am grateful to you, my dear. My intention was to inquire whether I could remain in your home. Returning to that place was something I wished to avoid, as it would feel as though I were stepping once more into the coldness and gloom of my former existence. Oh, Nell, Nell, you have proved to be such an incredible friend—'a good, sweet woman—true and faithful and to be depended on’—as Captain Saul described you.”
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0031 }

“He uttered ‘women,’ rather than ‘woman,’” Nell smiled. “It may be that Captain Saul views the two of us via the rose-colored glasses of his affection for us. Nevertheless, we are able to endeavor to fulfill his faith in us, anyway.”
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0032 }

“Do you recall, Nell,” Lorna murmured deliberately, “how I mentioned—the evening our paths crossed on the beach—that my attractive appearance was something I despised? At that time, I truly did. I was convinced that had I been plain, Rufus wouldn't have given me a second thought. My allure was repulsive to me since it drew him in, yet at present—oh, my looks bring me joy. They represent the sole gift I can present to Adrian,—and his artistic nature revels in them. It makes me sense that I am not arriving before him completely without a offering.”
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0033 }

“Adrian is in love with your beauty, Lorna, as anyone would be. However, you are being silly to state or believe that your beauty is the sole thing you offer him. HE is going to inform you of that, so there is no need for me to do so. I have to lock up at this point. Tabitha was expected to return this evening by me, yet she is absent.”
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0034 }

“Oh, yes, here I am, Mrs. Doctor, dear,” stated Tabitha, coming in without warning from the kitchen, “and blowing like a hen pulling rails at that! Coming down here from the Glen is quite a walk.”
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0035 }

“It pleases me that you have returned, Tabitha. What is the state of your sister’s health?”
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0036 }

“Though she can sit up, walking is still out of the question for her, naturally. Even so, she can manage quite fine without my help at present, since her vacationing daughter has returned home. Mrs. Doctor, dear, I am truly grateful to return. There was certainly no doubt about Matilda’s leg being broken, yet her tongue remained completely fine. Mrs. Doctor, dear, even if I am saddened to speak this way about my sister, she would talk endlessly without stopping. Her chatter was always constant, nevertheless she married before any of us in our family. Her feelings about marrying James Clow were actually quite indifferent, but she simply lacked the heart to refuse him. I am not saying James is not a decent man—my sole grievance regarding him, Mrs. Doctor, dear, is the eerie groan he invariably utters when beginning to offer thanks before meals. My appetite is invariably scared right off by it. And on the subject of weddings, Mrs. Doctor, dear, does truth lie in the rumor that Winifred Tolley will marry Ambrose Kerr?”
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0037 }

“Indeed, that is correct, Tabitha.”
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0038 }

“Indeed, Mrs. Doctor, dear, it DOES NOT appear just to me. Here I am, having never uttered a single word opposing men, yet I am completely unable to marry. On the other hand, Winifred Tolley constantly criticizes them, yet she only needs to extend her hand to take one, so to speak. Mrs. Doctor, dear, the world is remarkably peculiar.”
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0039 }

“Tabitha, you know there is another world.”
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0040 }

“Indeed,” Tabitha uttered while sighing deeply, “and yet, Mrs. Doctor, my dear, no one is married or given in marriage in that place.”
{: #nw-v04-c38-p0041 }
